capabilities.title: Local application platform and persistence
capabilities.scope: One local modular application serves the complete household product in both a Supervisor-managed App and standalone Docker from the first release. Home Assistant owns user authentication; Domus owns its business records.

readiness.blockingDecisions: Storage concurrency verification; supported Home Assistant release matrix; backup retention and restore targets. The owner selected Python/FastAPI, SQLite, one household per installation and a thin HA integration on 2026-10-29.

capabilities.title: Household members, Home Assistant identity and permissions
capabilities.scope: Each participating person uses their own Home Assistant account. Domus associates that verified user with one household member and applies explicit backend permissions independently of an optional person entity.

readiness.blockingDecisions: Detailed permission matrix/override review; authenticated recovery after external HA account loss; proof of HA identity/administrator status in both deployment targets; technical service principal policy. The owner confirmed three administrator-mapping modes with all HA administrators as the default, plus configurable household profiles and per-member permission exceptions.

capabilities.title: Task definitions, occurrences and household execution
capabilities.scope: Members create and perform household responsibilities with explicit assignments, actual performers and history. A recurring definition survives completion of each individual occurrence.

readiness.blockingDecisions: Detailed role/override review; first-release advanced task-type matrix. The owner confirmed role-default verification, material-completion handling and preservation of completed downstream work/points when its prerequisite is reopened on 2026-10-29.

capabilities.title: Recurrence engine and family calendar
capabilities.scope: A bounded scheduler turns task definitions into stable occurrences and a family calendar distinguishes planned start, deadline and actual completion.

readiness.blockingDecisions: Supported RRULE subset, time-zone/gap/fold library interoperability and calendar projection review. The owner confirmed first-instant execution for repeated local times with a household-configurable second-instant option, alongside gap advancement, actual-completion anchoring, successor/missed-work defaults and previewed future rule edits.

capabilities.title: Auditable points, participation and optional rewards
capabilities.scope: Task completion produces auditable point entries. Household-configurable collaboration policies determine each share and the actual award total; corrections preserve history and optional rewards never control basic participation.

readiness.blockingDecisions: Detailed remainder/override review; child-facing review. The owner confirmed configurable allocation, role-default verification, actual-work reporting, factual negative balances and a funding hold on approved/unfulfilled redemptions without sufficient backing after reversal.

capabilities.title: Shared shopping demand, purchases and receipt
capabilities.scope: Shopping combines manual intent, replenishment and task materials without losing provenance. Buying an item and physically receiving it are separate recorded facts.

readiness.blockingDecisions: Detailed demand-coverage and unit fixtures; partial-receipt UX; price/currency precision; launch purchase-session scope. The owner confirmed manual-extra and duplicate-safe automatic consolidation defaults on 2026-10-29.

capabilities.title: Product catalog, pantry stock and replenishment
capabilities.scope: The household knows what is available, where it is stored and what needs replenishment through a local product catalog and an immutable stock movement ledger.

readiness.blockingDecisions: Unit/package policy; reservation/replenishment review; barcode library/device evidence; external lookup provider feasibility, terms and response contract. The owner confirmed barcode scope, adjustable material recording and pending regularization rather than negative stock for task material shortfalls on 2026-10-29.

capabilities.title: Home Assistant entities, services and integration
capabilities.scope: Domus exposes its household capabilities as native Home Assistant entities, services and events. The already integrated HA MCP consumes these surfaces; no gateway work or second MCP is included.

readiness.blockingDecisions: Public service schemas and scope review; technical principal authorization; response-service exposure contract; supported HA matrix.

capabilities.title: Responsive application, household dashboard and navigation
capabilities.scope: A complete household interface serves all six domains from the first release with fast daily actions, responsive navigation and clear operation results, independently of entity dashboards and AI.

readiness.blockingDecisions: Detailed design system review; real mobile/companion and public host-context evidence; accessibility acceptance. The owner selected Lit/TypeScript/Vite, HA-coherent owned components, Storybook and Playwright on 2026-10-29.

capabilities.title: Clean Architecture, CI Check and isolated Stable and Edge channels
capabilities.scope: Every implemented capability starts with meaningful tests and enforced architecture boundaries. A CI Check workflow validates each PR update, and both deployment targets ship isolated experimental and production channels.

readiness.blockingDecisions: Runner/toolchain review; required-check configuration by maintainer; channel IDs and integration coexistence review; release publication authorization.

capabilities.title: Household automation engine and simple/advanced rule editors
capabilities.scope: Simple/default and optional advanced editors share one durable declarative automation engine in the first release, invoking authorized household commands with replay-safe execution and visible traces.

readiness.blockingDecisions: Detailed DSL/action catalog, numeric resource limits, external-effect receipts and supported HA/browser evidence. The owner confirmed both editors, one engine and disablement that stops new runs/later steps while retaining already-started atomic commands and effects.
